actions.text: arXiv:2611.12831 uses two implicit particle updates, a midpoint discretization of the coordinate equations and a spacetime Boris scheme (main.tex L401); its implicit-midpoint pusher is solved by fixed-point iteration that stops when the largest change of any endpoint component falls below 1e-7 in code units (L459), and in the Kerr tests a convergence threshold of 2e-14 is enforced on the nonlinear iterations (L775).
actions.label: fulltext

actions.text: arXiv:2505.03934 notes that the main results on N-body scattering come from very many simulations, often more than hundreds of thousands or millions, a major challenge for expensive numerical-relativity simulations (apssamp.tex L108), and therefore runs a few selected binary-single and binary-binary case studies with the code BAM (L110), with all black-hole masses equal, so that the single hole has half the mass of the binary (L246).
actions.label: fulltext

actions.text: arXiv:2602.06961 (Heinze, Schaefer, Bruegmann) gives the general N-body 2PN Hamiltonian in ADM gauge and integrates its equations of motion (pn-nbody code); arXiv:2610.20594 (Heinze, Cao) constrains the outer orbit of a hierarchical black-hole triple from two merger events with Peters equations and integrates with the same pn-nbody code (L1469); it is not itself a PN N-body dynamics paper. Both share an author with the BAM binary-single study arXiv:2505.03934.
actions.label: fulltext
